name: Roccavento - The Fire at the Mountain Pass
description: The reference wildfire scenario for the Roccavento Island exercise ("medium" case): the fire starts above Le Terrazze at 13:00, with an east-southeasterly wind at 36 km/h and very dry fine fuels (5% moisture). It is not reported until 13:30. At 13:45 the wind shifts to the northeast, driving the fire front toward the mountain pass and Pian dei Grilli. Three player roles, 30-minute turns, six villages and approximately 1,500 residents. The island has no overland exit and all reinforcements come from the mainland. Times, equipment, capacities and response parameters are exercise assumptions.

edits.description: Entirely fictional 8 x 8 km island (from propagator_abm): six villages, a ridge with a mountain pass, a fortress on the summit, a port on the eastern coast, and cliffs along the rest of the coastline. No real-world geography.

actions.note: "Medium" exercise case: the fire has already been burning for 30 minutes when it is reported.
actions.title: Ignition in the pinewood above Le Terrazze

actions.note: Uncertain estimate based on residents' calls.
actions.title: Initial estimate from emergency calls

msel.objective: Make an initial assessment despite incomplete information and an already established fire. EXCON note: ignition is a pre-scheduled action that runs automatically at 13:00 (exercise start). The approximate fire estimate reads the actual simulated fire; if ignition is disabled, the estimate must also be disabled.
msel.text: 13:30. Several Le Terrazze residents have called to report a column of smoke rising from the pinewood above the village, toward the ridge. The fire has probably been burning for some time; no one saw it start. Its mapped location is estimated from the calls and should be treated as indicative only.
msel.title: Smoke above Le Terrazze

actions.note: At 13:45, as in the "medium" case (45 minutes after ignition).
actions.title: Wind shifts to the northeast

msel.objective: Assess whether the forecast wind shift is taken into account in plans for Pian dei Grilli and Le Ghiande, beyond the mountain pass, before it actually occurs.
msel.text: 13:31. East-southeasterly wind at 36 km/h; fine fuel moisture is 5%. Within the next 15-30 minutes, the wind is expected to shift to the northeast without changing speed. The flow will be channelled along the ridge toward the mountain pass.
msel.title: Weather bulletin: wind shift

msel.objective: Assess how the incident command allocates its limited crews and whether it requests reinforcements from the mainland without delay.
msel.text: 13:50. Crews arriving from Castelvento report tall flames in the scrub along Strada del Passo and confirm that the wind is now from the northeast. A timestamped survey of burning and adjacent areas is available on the map.
msel.title: First crews on scene

msel.objective: Test priorities among villages, selection of evacuation destinations, and how to handle residents refusing to leave. EXCON note: evacuation proceeds one village at a time and assembly areas must be opened. Decisions concerning Le Ghiande remain narrative rather than system-enforced.
msel.text: 14:00. Farmers living in isolated homes around Le Ghiande say they intend to stay to protect their livestock. The village has no assembly area of its own; meanwhile, many Le Terrazze residents are asking where they should go.
msel.title: Le Ghiande residents refuse to leave

msel.objective: Test the trade-off between bringing in reinforcements and providing shelter, and coordination between the municipality and operations centre. EXCON note: the outcome is narrative; reinforcements still follow approved requests.
msel.text: 14:30. The scheduled ferry can dock at the port within one hour. On this trip it can either bring reinforcements from the mainland or accommodate up to 300 people from San Rocco on board. It cannot do both.
msel.title: The port and the ferry

msel.objective: Ensure public communication is consistent with decisions already taken and the responsible roles coordinate their statements before going on air.
msel.text: 15:00. Island Radio will go on air in ten minutes and wants to know which villages are being evacuated, where residents should go, and whether roads to the port remain open. A photo of the fortress shrouded in smoke is circulating on social media.
msel.title: Island Radio requests an update

msel.objective: Take stock of the situation: what has changed, what remains exposed, and which additional reinforcements are still needed.
msel.text: 15:30. A consolidated, up-to-date picture is now available for burning and adjacent areas: fire, buildings, roads, fire lines and deployed units. Use it for the operations centre situation briefing.
msel.title: Consolidated situation report
